title: Where does the lift stop in each of the seven rides?
description: Seven lift rides are given, each with a starting floor and a button press. Each ride is counted floor by floor, up for plus and down for minus, and one ride is checked by going back.
teaching_notes: One idea: starting floor plus movement gives the target floor. Watch for students who think adding always takes the lift higher, even with a minus press.

video_script.why: The child reads each sum as a starting floor and a press, and finds the floor where the lift stops.
video_script.substitution: the book's own seven rides read as starting floor plus movement
video_script.anchor: the lift in {{NAME_10}}, with seven rides of a starting floor and a press
video_script.payoff_line: Starting floor plus movement gives the target floor.

final_answer.spoken: the lift stops at plus five, plus five, plus one, plus one, zero, plus two and minus two

names.{{NAME_10}}: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

never_show: a minus press taking the lift higher
video_script.design: One idea: each sum is a lift ride. One lift picture throughout; the floors are counted along the side. Method as in the solved example.

beats.on_screen: title card Seven Lift Rides; the lift of the tall block appears with seven rides listed, each a starting floor and a button press

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the lift appears
marks.rides: the seven rides are listed in the anchor band
marks.ask: the question is written into the anchor band

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the lift in {{NAME_10}}.
<bookmark mark='rides'/>Seven lift rides are given, each with a starting floor and a button press.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>On which floor does the lift stop each time?

beats.on_screen: the seven rides stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the child thinks

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the lift beside a floor line; an up arrow marks plus presses and a down arrow marks minus presses; the first number of a ride is tagged starting floor and the second number is tagged press

marks.rule: the two parts of a ride are tagged on the board
marks.way: the solved example from the book is shown beside the lift
marks.dir: the up arrow and the down arrow are drawn beside the lift

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Each ride has a starting floor and a button press.
<bookmark mark='way'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='dir'/>Plus presses go up, and minus presses go down.

marks.given: the line Given is written with the seven rides

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, seven rides.
The first number is the starting floor, and the second number is the press.

beats.on_screen: To find: the floor where the lift stops in each ride

marks.find: the line To find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the floor where the lift stops in each ride.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: both presses go up: (+1) + (+4) = +5 and (+4) + (+1) = +5

marks.up: the first two rides are circled
marks.five: the lift rises from plus one to plus five and then from plus four to plus five

narration: <bookmark mark='up'/>Step one, take the first two rides, where both presses go up.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Four floors up from plus one reaches plus five.
One floor up from plus four reaches plus five too.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: (+4) + (−3), minus means down, count 3 floors down from +4: +3, +2, +1, so +1

marks.down: a down arrow of three floors is drawn from plus four and each floor is lit

narration: <bookmark mark='ride'/>Step two, the third ride starts on plus four and presses minus three.
<bookmark mark='down'/>Minus means down, so count three floors down.
Plus three, plus two, and then plus one.

marks.below: the fourth and fifth rides are circled and minus one is tagged
marks.two: the lift rises two floors from minus one
marks.one: the lift rises one floor from minus one

narration: <bookmark mark='below'/>Step three, the next two rides start below the ground, on minus one.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Plus two goes two floors up, to zero and then plus one.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Plus one goes one floor up, to zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 0 + (+2) = +2 and 0 + (−2) = −2, start on the ground floor

marks.start: the last two rides are circled and the ground floor is tagged 0
marks.up2: the lift rises two floors from the ground floor
marks.down2: the lift drops two floors from the ground floor

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Step four, the last two rides start on the ground floor, which is zero.
<bookmark mark='up2'/>Plus two goes two floors up, to plus two.
<bookmark mark='down2'/>Minus two goes two floors down, to minus two.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check the third ride, from +1 go back up 3 floors: +2, +3, +4

marks.check: the lift climbs three floors from plus one
marks.back: floor plus four lights up as the starting floor

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the third ride by going back up three floors from plus one.
<bookmark mark='back'/>That reaches plus four, where the ride began.

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed on the working board
marks.pay: the three parts of the rule are shown together

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The lift stops at plus five, plus five, plus one, plus one, zero, plus two and minus two.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Starting floor plus movement gives the target floor.
